pool.text: The Song court opened a maritime trade office there to manage the shipping trade.
The temple to the sea goddess Tianhou was built and houses a museum.
The Qing decided to fortify Jiao'ao as a defense against naval attacks.
Commercial interests established the Germania Brewery which later became the world-famous Tsingtao Brewery.
Sun Yat-sen visited the Tsingtao area and stated that he was impressed.
China agreed to recognize Japan's special position through the Twenty-One Demands.
A notable Neo-romanesque church designed by German architect Alfred Fräbel was completed.
Japan re-occupied Qingdao a year after expanding the Second Sino-Japanese War.
During the Chinese Civil War the city was taken by Chairman Mao Zedong.
The Chinese government named a district of Qingdao a Special Economic and Technology Development Zone.
Bandao Broadcasting Media Corporation, a news and broadcasting agency was founded.
Guitar manufacturers Epiphone opened a factory in Qingdao.
The annual cargo handling capacity exceeded 100 million tons for the first time.
The city's GDP reached 42.3 billion, ranking first in Shandong Province.
Qingdao was named as one of China's top ten cities by brand value.
Qingdao and Beijing cohosted the Olympic Sailing competitions during the Summer Olympics.
Qingdao was named China's most livable city by the Chinese Institute of City Competitiveness.
The longest bridge over water opened in Qingdao.
Jiaonan city merged into Huangdao District after approval.
All public transportation companies use Qingdaotong Card with the last company starting it.
